switch-expression.md:48 'In most cases, the compiler generates a warning if a switch expression doesn't handle all possible input values.' A string has unbounded values, so the compiler can at most warn about missing coverage in general (no discard), not about one missing kind; a switch statement or a switch with a discard compiles silently.

issues.quote: One shared method holding the `switch` removes the copies; while the fee is the only question, that can be enough. Then a second question about the kind, such as the delivery time, needs its own `switch`.
issues.text: I re-read this paragraph twice. 'Then' reads like the next event in the story, but the situation never mentioned delivery time, so I was unsure whether it is a hypothetical. The link from 'the kind is a string' to 'the compiler does not notice a miss' also only lands once the next-but-one paragraph says classes do compile-check.
issues.fix: Replace 'Then a second question' with 'But once a second question', and end the paragraph with 'With one class per kind, as the next paragraphs show, the compiler does notice.'

issues.quote: `StandardShipping` already names `ShippingFee` after its `:`, and a C# class can name only one class there, so it cannot also derive from an invoice-line class.
issues.text: I had to reconstruct the middle step: why would StandardShipping want to derive from an 'invoice-line class' at all? The text jumps from 'both must answer one shared call' to 'cannot also derive', without saying that the base-type way would need both classes to derive from one shared base.
issues.fix: Add one sentence before this one: 'With a base type, both would have to derive from one shared invoice-line class.'
